The courtyard parking hemmed by older Austro-Hungarian-style roofs, worn stucco and a striped awning, with a modern curved glass tower rising behind, fits a compact Central European capital. The mix of old tile roofs plus that contemporary glass high-rise is most consistent with Ljubljana, Slovenia.

Right-hand traffic, Cyrillic/Latin billboard and shop signage, and the broad Soviet/post-earthquake avenue with four-storey blocks fit Tashkent better than Samarkand or Bukhara. text:

>>> {"country":"Myanmar","place":"Mandalay","lat":21.9750,"lng":96.0830}
